A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same TIE scheduler. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices are readable and support reliable matching, including relocated material.

before.justification: v1 reports original distribution-fitting results, online and offline scheduling benchmarks, ablations, and additional-model experiments.

after.justification: v2 retains those original results and adds prompt-family diagnostics, sensitivity experiments, prediction-noise tests, and a TRAIL comparison.

M1.justification: The DeBERTa predictor, log-t parameterization, training strategy, censored expectation/CVaR score, adaptive beta, starvation prevention, and asynchronous scheduling procedure remain unchanged. New experiments test existing components.

E1.justification: Both versions use LMSYS-Chat-1M, ShareGPT, and Alpaca for online chatbot serving and offline synthetic data generation. New prompt-family diagnostics reuse existing samples, while sensitivity tests vary configurations within retained coverage. OpenPanGu results already appeared in v1.

E2.justification: v2 newly evaluates TRAIL against TIE in Appendix D.8, Table 11; v1 only discussed TRAIL. The main FCFS, SSJF, and LTR comparator set and existing distribution/score ablation variants are retained.

E3.justification: Appendices D.4–D.9 add substantial experimental protocols: prompt classification, training-data budget controls, training at temperature 0.7 with evaluation at 0.4–1.6, fixed-beta comparisons across loads, and multiplicative sigma perturbations. These extend evaluation rather than revise the original benchmarks' stated settings.

E4.justification: v2 adds prompt-family tail diagnostics, training-scale sensitivity, temperature generalization, adaptive-versus-fixed-beta comparisons across loads, and prediction-noise robustness. These substantially broaden analysis beyond v1's distribution/score ablations, repetition-count and degrees-of-freedom studies, and scheduling heatmaps.

E5.justification: Existing repeated-generation fitting and KS testing are retained. v2 introduces no new repeated-evaluation counts, seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance-testing procedures. The new generations-per-prompt settings concern training-data budgets.

E6.justification: Tables 7–12 add extensive diagnostic and sensitivity results while retaining earlier benchmark values, including relocated OpenPanGu results. For example, Table 11 reports TIE/TRAIL latency of 0.67/1.41 s/token at 100 RPS; Table 12 shows TIE at 1.66 versus LTR at 1.55 under maximum sigma noise at 100 RPS.

T1.justification: Assumption 3.1, Theorem 3.2, the method equations, and the proofs and censored-distribution derivations in Appendices A–B are unchanged. The new learning-augmented discussion is conceptual and adds no formal theorem or proof.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, and conclusion retain the same claims about distributional output-length prediction, log-t modeling, risk-aware TIE scheduling, and online/offline performance and generalization. Additional experiments support those retained contributions.

C2.justification: v2 adds a consistency–robustness interpretation of expectation/CVaR, explains classical scheduling assumptions that fail in LLM serving, and discusses training-cost amortization, temperature degradation, noise tolerance, and preemption overhead. The training-data limitation itself is retained from v1's Appendix E and moved into Section 7.

D1.justification: v2 adds an explicit TIE repository link, specifies single-GPU deployment for OpenPanGu, and identifies Qwen3-32B in thinking mode as the prompt classifier. These improve access and implementation documentation without establishing changes to the retained method or deployments.

R1.justification: v2 expands the existing SEPT connection through a stochastic-scheduling paragraph and adds learning-augmented-algorithm positioning with new references. It also adds model and contextual citations and removes the TensorRT-LLM reference. These are focused extensions of the retained LLM-scheduling positioning.

P1.justification: Localized structural edits remove the introductory existing-solutions paragraph, add Discussion and Acknowledgements, revise the impact statement, move limitations into the main text, and consolidate OpenPanGu material. Most existing technical prose remains unchanged.

P2.justification: Six new appendix tables provide substantial new diagnostic and sensitivity displays. v1's separate OpenPanGu Tables 7–8 are merged into Tables 5–6. The ten existing figures and main Tables 1–4 are retained, with only minor positioning and pagination changes.

improvement.justification: v1 discussed preemption costs without evaluating a preemptive comparator and acknowledged training-data costs without an end-to-end data-efficiency study. v2 directly addresses both gaps through Tables 8 and 11, alongside substantial robustness validation. The results expose useful boundaries, including TRAIL's advantage at 30–40 RPS and TIE's loss to LTR under maximum noise. These gains outweigh a limited editorial regression: Section 2 still references the deleted introductory baseline discussion.
